newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's real rises 0.03 pct in seesaw trade.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's real rises 0.03 pct in seesaw trade.

text.p: Brazil's real rose 0.03 percent in volatile trade on the commercial foreign exchange market to close at 1.0392 per dollar, dealers said.
They said market movement was similar to Thursday's trade, with players reacting to dollar inflows and outflows, leading the real to fluctuate between 1.0370 and 1.0400 per greenback.
But unlike Thursday, preliminary figures for commercial and financial forex contracts showed a Friday surplus of around $200 million. On Thursday net dollar flows registred a $50.1 million deficit.
However, dealers believe Friday's surplus would be lower when the day's total contracts are registered.
The market expects a new drop in the real-dollar mini-band in coming days. Dealers said the Central Bank could lower the mini-band at least 0.15 percent next week.
The current mini-band was set on December 10 between 1.0360 and 1.0410 reais per dollar.
In the floating exchange rate market, the real dropped 0.03 percent to close at 1.0420 per dollar.
In the illegal parallel market, the real ended at 1.117 per greenback, down 0.18 percent.
